initialNotebook.lightContent:
Notebooks are perfect for capturing the loose threads that become your story.

Use this space for:
- Character backstories and motivations
- Scene ideas and dialogue snippets
- Plot twists and "what if" questions
- Research, references, and inspiration
- World-building details and locations

Come back anytime to drop a new thought.
initialNotebook.darkContent:
A novel lives in the details. Keep the important ones close.

Use this space for:
- Chapter outlines and story beats
- Timelines and character ages
- Settings, maps, and geography
- Themes, motifs, and symbols
- Revision notes and feedback to yourself

Let this notebook grow as your story grows.

hero.title: StoryMode — Creative Writing Studio and World-Building Tools
hero.sub: A calm place to write your story and a fun way to build your world. With a helpful editor by your side, folios full of ideas, interactive timelines, and maps that spring to life.

write.title: Disappear into the draft.
write.body: A full-bleed page that gets out of the way. With an AI editor that waits in the margin: it tightens a line, flags a mixed metaphor, points out a plothole. Writing is all yours.

organize.title: A home for your ideas.
organize.body: Characters, factions, locations, history: all kept in folios you open like apps. Reorder the outline on a board, then watch the whole saga fall into place on a timeline.

map.title: Draw your own territory.
map.body: Sketch coastlines and roads by hand, or describe a place and let Storymode render it. AI Draw in pixel, painterly, or flat styles. Map your world as fast as you can picture it.

guide.title: Guide
guide.subtitle: Everything you need to know about writing, planning, mapping and collaborating in StoryMode.

useCases.p1: Chat works two ways: book-wide when nothing is selected, and grounded on a passage when you highlight text in a chapter first. Use book-wide to reason across your whole manuscript: continuity, character arcs, pacing between chapters.
useCases.p2: Ask about a single character's behaviour — "Is Lia's behaviour here consistent with how she acts in previous chapters?" — and Chat weighs it against every earlier scene, then answers with a verdict, moments that ring true, and small wobbles worth smoothing.
useCases.p3: Hunt for plot holes, timeline slips, or information gaps across multiple chapters at once. Chat distinguishes real contradictions from deliberate mysteries you're seeding, and points at the exact lines it's reasoning from.
useCases.p4: Highlight a paragraph and Chat narrows to just that passage — perfect for a targeted editorial pass on clarity, voice, tone, rhythm, or craft. It comes back with clear sections and concrete rewrite options in the author's voice.
useCases.p5: Other things Chat handles well: finding where a location or item was first mentioned, brainstorming alternate scenes, summarizing tangled lore for a synopsis, and comparing events across timelines.

getting-started.title: Getting Started
getting-started.intro: StoryMode organizes your work as Projects → Folios → Notebooks. Every new account begins with a fully populated example project so you can explore before starting your own.

dashboard.title: The Dashboard
dashboard.body: The dashboard shows all your projects as large cards. Click a project to open it — you can then switch between Folios, Timeline and Map views from the header.

projects.title: Projects, Folios & Notebooks
projects.body: Projects are your books, games, or campaigns. Inside each Project, Folios group related notebooks (Characters, Places, Chapters, Lore…). Notebooks are the individual notes.

starter.title: The Starter Project
starter.body: New accounts receive a copy of “A Study in Scarlet” pre-populated with folios, timeline events and a world map so you can see every feature in action.

themes.title: Themes
themes.intro: StoryMode uses a minimalist dark aesthetic, but you can customize the look of individual notebooks — and tune the editor to match your reading comfort.

notebook-theme.title: Notebook Theme
notebook-theme.body: Each notebook card in a Folio can be assigned its own theme. Themes change the card's background color, border, and accent tone so you can group related notes at a glance — for example, blue for characters, green for locations, or amber for lore. Open a notebook in the Folio grid and click the theme option to open the picker. The theme preview updates instantly so you can see how the card will look before saving. Pick a color that matches the notebook's purpose, then close the picker to apply it.

editor-theme.title: Editor Theme
editor-theme.body: You can also choose the theme for your Story Editor and Focus Mode, tinting the writing surface so that you can start with a blank, white page or a moody dark theme. The chosen theme carries into the Story Editor and Focus Mode, tinting the writing surface so long chapters feel visually tied to the notebook they belong to.

font-size.title: Font & Size
font-size.body: Adjust the editor font size to match your screen and eyesight. Larger sizes work well for long drafting sessions or high-resolution displays, while smaller sizes let you fit more of the chapter on screen when revising structure. Then choose the typeface used for writing: pick a serif for a book-like feel, a clean sans-serif for a modern editor look, or a monospaced face for a screenplay/manuscript feel. Font and size apply across the Story Editor and Focus Mode; the rest of the app keeps its consistent UI typography.

story-editor.title: Story Editor & Chapters
story-editor.intro: The Story view is a focused, long-form writing environment for Chapter notebooks with autosave, keyboard shortcuts and a rich Markdown editor.

focus.title: Focus Mode
focus.body: Open Focus Mode to hide the surrounding UI and write in a calm, full-screen editor. The margins, folios, and tools fade away, leaving just your text and the cursor so you can disappear into the draft.

formatting.title: Writing & Formatting
formatting.body:
Use the floating toolbar to bold, italicize, underline, add headings and quotes. The toolbar exposes bold, italic, inline code, headings (H1–H3) and block quotes — every action applies to the current selection or the line the cursor is on.

Keyboard shortcuts: Cmd/Ctrl+B for bold, Cmd/Ctrl+I for italic, and Cmd/Ctrl+Z / Shift+Cmd/Ctrl+Z for undo and redo.

autosave.title: Autosave & Draft Status
autosave.body: StoryMode saves your draft every 15 seconds while you type and again whenever you leave the editor. A subtle status indicator shows when a save is in flight and when the draft is safely stored, so you never wonder if your last edit made it.

scroll-memory.title: Scroll Memory
scroll-memory.body: When you leave and return to a chapter, StoryMode restores your exact scroll position — even after switching projects or reloading the browser. Great for picking up mid-paragraph on long chapters.

history.title: Undo History & Recovering Edits
history.body: The editor keeps a full in-session undo history: use Cmd/Ctrl+Z to step back through recent edits and Shift+Cmd/Ctrl+Z to redo. Because autosave writes continuously, closing the tab and reopening restores the latest saved draft automatically.

chapters.title: Adding & Deleting Chapters
chapters.body: Create a chapter from the Folios browser — it opens straight into edit mode with the 📝 icon already set. Deleting a chapter requires a two-click confirmation within 3 seconds to protect against mistakes.

ai-editor.title: AI Editor
ai-editor.intro: The AI Editor is a second pair of eyes that works while you do. Select a passage, mark it for review, and keep writing — the feedback will be waiting when you’re ready.

opinions.title: Review while you write
opinions.body: Select any passage in a chapter and click Mark for Review. The AI Editor works in the background, so you can keep reading, writing, or reviewing other passages while it thinks. Each note costs a few credits, scaled to the length of the passage. When it’s ready, the note appears in the AI Editor sidebar with a critique and one or more rewrite suggestions you can replace with a single click.

feedback-examples.title: What the feedback looks like
feedback-examples.body:
The AI Editor flags what feels off and explains why, then gives concrete rewrite suggestions you can compare. A few examples of the kind of notes it leaves:

- “This sentence repeats ‘slowly’ and ‘quietly’ — try condensing the action to heighten tension.”
- “The dialogue tag is redundant because the line itself conveys the emotion; consider removing it.”
- “This description is vivid but interrupts the pacing. Try moving it to a moment when the character has time to notice.”

Each note also shows the original passage in context, so you can tap Replace, copy a suggestion, or dismiss the note entirely.

chat.title: Chat with Your Story
chat.intro: Ask questions about characters, plot points, locations or lore. Chat has read access to all of your project’s notebooks and timeline, so answers are grounded in your own world.

asking.title: Asking Questions
asking.body: Type a question in the chat panel. Responses cite the notebook(s) they came from so you can jump straight to the source. Short questions about the chapter you're in cost very little; book-wide questions (plot holes, continuity, arcs) read much more of your story and cost more credits.

selection.title: Grounding Answers in a Selection
selection.body: Highlight a passage in a chapter before asking a question and Chat will answer from that specific text, making feedback precise and contextual. Costs a few credits, depending on the length of the passage.

timeline.title: Timeline
timeline.intro: The Timeline lays your story’s events on a virtual, zoomable ribbon that spans a single day to millennia — perfect for fantasy and sci-fi worlds.

dates.title: Dates & Ranges
dates.body:
StoryMode accepts almost any date you can write: single dates like 2026-07-23, July 23, 2026, 23 July 2026, or far-future and far-past years like 3025 and 10,000 BC. For ranges, separate two dates with a dash or the word “to”: 3025-01-15 to 3025-06-30, Spring 3025 — Fall 3025, or 1500 BC - 1450 BC. Sci-fi and fantasy timelines are first-class citizens: you can use years like 12027 or -4832.

At the project level, the Timeline automatically aggregates events from every folio into a single view — each row is color-coded by the folio it belongs to, so you can see how characters, plotlines and world events line up across your entire story.

pan-zoom.title: Pan & Zoom
pan-zoom.body: Drag horizontally to pan across the ribbon. Scroll (or pinch) to zoom — StoryMode zooms toward the point under your cursor so you can dive from centuries down to a single day without losing your place. Zoom level and scroll position are remembered per folio.

previews.title: Event Previews
previews.body: Hover an event to see a floating preview with the full markdown snippet. The popup follows your cursor for extended-range events, and you can pin it open to keep reading while you scroll the timeline.

map.title: Map — Drawing Tools
map.intro: The Map is a canvas of terrain, notebooks and labels. Every tool lives in the left toolbar and is available via a single-key shortcut.

pointer.title: Pointer (V)
pointer.body: Select and move pills, resize stickers by dragging a corner handle, and press Delete to remove the selection.

pan.title: Pan (H)
pan.body: Drag to pan the canvas. Scroll to zoom toward the cursor. Use “View All” to frame every element at once.

pencil.title: Pencil & Color Picker (P)
pencil.body: Paint terrain cells one stroke at a time. The color picker opens beside the pencil with seven hue families and muted/vibrant shade rows, plus a custom HSL gradient and hex input for exact colors. Every color you actually apply is remembered in the recents row at the bottom of the picker — an MRU (most-recently-used) strip that keeps your last dozen colors one click away so you don't have to hunt for them again.

fill.title: Fill Bucket (F)
fill.body: Flood-fills an enclosed area. If the shape isn’t enclosed, it sets the map’s global background color instead.

eyedropper.title: Eyedropper (I)
eyedropper.body: Click any cell or background to sample its color — StoryMode then switches you back to the pencil so you can keep drawing.

brush.title: Brush Size
brush.body: Adjust brush radius from the floating picker. The cursor overlay always shows the exact area you’ll paint.

label.title: Label Tool (T)
label.body: Place a dashed-border text pill anywhere on the map to annotate regions, borders or landmarks.

notebook-pill.title: Place Notebooks (N)
notebook-pill.body: Pick any folio + notebook from the project and drop it as a pill. Search by title or contents. After placement the tool reverts to pointer.

delete-tool.title: Delete Tool (X)
delete-tool.body: Hover a pill to preview a red wiggle warning, then click to confirm removal with a themed explosion.

undo.title: Undo / Redo
undo.body: StoryMode keeps a 50-step history of every canvas edit so you can step back and forward through recent changes.

ai-draw.title: AI Draw
ai-draw.intro: Generate stickers for your map from natural-language prompts, in the illustrated storybook aesthetic that matches the rest of StoryMode.

stickers.title: Drawing Stickers on the Map
stickers.body: Pick AI Draw (A), describe what you want (a mossy tower, a market cart, a harbour lighthouse…) and drop the generated sticker anywhere on the map. Resize by dragging a corner handle, rotate with the puck, and press Delete to remove it. Each sticker costs around 16 credits. Styles: choose an illustrated sticker for a hand-painted storybook look, or a pixel sticker for a retro, blocky game-map feel. You can also steer the art direction in your prompt — watercolor, ink line art, flat illustration, woodcut, textured gouache — so every landmark matches the world you're building.

scan.title: Document Scan
scan.intro: Import handwritten or printed notes by uploading a photo or PDF — the AI transcribes it directly into a new notebook.

scanning.title: Scanning a Page
scanning.body: Open Scan from any folio, drop your file, and confirm the parsed text. Costs a few credits per scan.

sharing.title: Public & Private Projects
sharing.intro: Every project is either private (only you) or public (read-only for anyone with the link). Team sharing and collaboration features are temporarily disabled.

private.title: Private Projects
private.body: New projects are private by default. Only you can view and edit them. Folios, timelines, maps, and notes are not accessible to anyone else.

public.title: Public Read-only Links
public.body: Toggle a project to public from the project header to share the story, timeline, and map with anyone. Emails and private notes remain hidden.

plans-credits.title: Plans & Credits
plans-credits.intro: AI usage is metered in a single pool of credits. Every request costs credits based on how much work it takes, so a short chapter question is cheap while a book-wide analysis or an AI Draw sticker costs more. Each plan includes a monthly allowance; you can top up any time.

watching.title: Watching Your Balance
watching.body: Your Profile shows a progress bar for your credit balance. A global banner appears when you’re close to running out.

topups.title: Buying More Credits
topups.body: One-click top-ups from the Plans page. Admins can also grant credits directly from the admin dashboard.

byok.title: Bring Your Own OpenAI Key
byok.body:
Connect your own OpenAI API key in Profile → Integrations to bypass the StoryMode credit quota entirely. When a key is active, the AI Editor, Chat, AI Draw, and Scan all use your key’s balance instead of consuming StoryMode credits, so you never have to think about allowances, top-ups or monthly resets.

StoryMode automatically routes your requests to the strongest OpenAI models available on your key: the latest GPT-5 family for chat and review, and gpt-image-1 with high quality for AI Draw and stickers. That means you get the fastest, most capable output without the per-call credit cost.

Your key is encrypted at rest and is only decrypted inside StoryMode backend functions — it is never sent to the browser or stored in plain text. You can replace or remove it at any time. Note: AI Map Drawing and AI stickers require an OpenAI key with image-generation access; Anthropic Claude keys are not supported because Claude cannot generate images.

plans.title: Choosing a Plan
plans.body: Draft is free forever, Manuscript is $5/mo for regular writers, and Studio is $20/mo for heavy AI users.

welcome.heading: Write your story. Create your world.

editor.label: Story Editor
editor.title: A reader for your draft, on call at 2am.

map.label: Map Builder
map.title: Describe a location and watch it materialise.

folio.label: Folio of Ideas
folio.title: Everything you imagined, one click away.

folios.title: Folios: your project's boards of notes
folios.subtitle: A folio is a board of notebooks. Keep characters, places, research or scene ideas side by side, then reuse them across your timeline, maps and chapters.

notebooks.title: Write in notebooks
notebooks.body: Add notebooks in columns, drag to reorder, resize them, and give each one a paper theme.

timeline.title: See dates on a timeline
timeline.body: Give a notebook a date or a range and it appears on the folio timeline, and on the project timeline too.

mapStory.title: Use them on maps and in Story
mapStory.body: Drop folio notebooks onto a map as place pins, and keep them at hand while you draft chapters.

folios.createHint: It starts with two short notebooks of writing tips you can edit or delete.

folioEmpty.title: This folio is empty
folioEmpty.body: Notebooks are the notes inside a folio: a character sketch, a location, a scene idea. Add your first one to get going.
folioEmpty.hint: Use New column in the header to place notebooks side by side.

foliosModal.heading: Your characters, places and research, all in one place.
foliosModal.intro: Tell us what your story needs and we will set it up now, with a few examples to start you off. Everything you write here follows you: onto your timeline, onto your maps, and beside your draft.
foliosModal.footnote: The notes are just examples. Rewrite them, or throw them out.

characters.title: Characters
characters.body: Who they are, what they want, when they were born.

notes.content:
Name:

Wants:

Fears:

Born: 

First appears in:

notes.content:
Name:

What they want that the protagonist cannot allow:

How they justify it:

notes.content:
Name:

How they met:

What they risk:

notes.title: Cast list
notes.content: One line each for everyone else who speaks.

locations.title: Locations
locations.body: Every place your story visits, ready to pin on a map.

notes.title: Home
notes.content: Where the story starts. What it smells like, who is always there.

notes.title: The road
notes.content: Places passed through on the way to the ending.

notes.title: The place it ends
notes.content: What must be true here for the story to finish.

scenes.title: Scenes
scenes.body: Loose scene cards you can shuffle into chapters.

notes.title: The turn
notes.content: The moment there is no going back.

notes.title: The cost
notes.content: What is lost to get what is wanted.

notes.title: Last page
notes.content: The final beat, even if it changes later.

research.title: Research
research.body: The facts and quotes you keep looking up twice.

notes.title: Facts to check
notes.content: Dates, distances, names and anything you guessed.

notes.title: Quotes and sources
notes.content: Lines worth keeping, with where they came from.

factions.title: Factions and lore
factions.body: Houses, orders and guilds, and who owes whom.

notes.title: Powers
notes.content: Who rules what, and how they hold it.

notes.title: Debts and grudges
notes.content: Who owes whom, and since when.

notes.title: Rules of this world
notes.content: What is possible here that is not possible elsewhere.

timelineModal.heading: See your whole story in order, without building a thing.
timelineModal.intro: Date anything, anywhere in your project, a character, an event, a chapter, and it appears here on its own.
timelineModal.footnote: Real years, invented ones, or an era you name yourself.

mapModal.heading: Draw the world your story happens in.
mapModal.intro: Sketch it yourself or have AI illustrate it for you, then pin your characters and places straight onto it.

hand.title: Draw it by hand
hand.body: Pencil, colours and a fill bucket for coastlines and forests. Name your cities and roads, and drop any note onto the map as a pin.

ai.title: Or describe it and let AI illustrate
ai.body: Ask for a castle, a harbour, an airship. It arrives in seconds, in one of three styles, so the whole map holds together.
